prompt:
# Subject Merge Fine Clustering

## Quick Start

Inside one topic area, create tight candidate clusters that are worth a later same-concept decision. Use only the provided candidate cards.

## Identity Filter

Cluster candidates only when they might be the same teachable idea at the same level, testable with the same question.

Do not cluster just because candidates share a keyword. Keep candidates separate when one adds implementation, math, limitation, application, deeper mechanism, tool-specific behavior, or a broader/narrower student action.

Doubt means singleton. Under-clustering is safer than sending unrelated candidates to merge evaluation.

## Output

Return one JSON object only:

```json
{
  "clusters": [
    {
      "id": "cluster_001",
      "label": "Short candidate cluster",
      "rationale": "Why these candidates may share concept identity.",
      "candidate_ids": ["candidate-id"]
    }
  ]
}
```

## Self-Check

- Every input candidate ID appears exactly once.
- Each non-singleton cluster has a plausible same-concept reason.
- Implementation, limitation, application, math, and deeper-revisit candidates were not grouped with definitions just because labels overlap.
- Mixed-language same-level candidates were clustered when their teachable idea matches.
- No web search or external knowledge was used.

area.label: Text Preprocessing and Tokenization
area.rationale: Focuses on initial text processing steps: segmentation, tokenization, stop word removal, cleaning, and encoding handling.

candidates.label: Text Preprocessing: Segmentation, Tokenization, and Stop Words
candidates.description: The initial NLP steps: breaking documents into sentences (segmentation), sentences into words (tokenization), and removing common stop words to focus on meaningful content.
coverage_criteria: Explain segmentation, tokenization, and the role of stop words in NLP preprocessing.
candidates.lesson_title: Introdução ao Processamento de Linguagem Natural

candidates.label: Text Preprocessing: Tokenization and Stopword Removal
candidates.description: Tokenization splits text into individual words (tokens). Stopwords are common low-information words that are often removed to reduce noise and vocabulary size. NLTK provides built-in stopword lists.
coverage_criteria: Write code to remove stopwords using NLTK.
candidates.lesson_title: Representação de palavras e "Bag of Words" (BoW)

candidates.label: Tokenization with NLTK
candidates.description: Understanding tokenization as converting text into a list of words and punctuation, and using nltk.word_tokenize for better handling of contractions than simple regex splitting.
coverage_criteria: Recognizes that NLTK represents tokenized text as a list of string tokens.
Uses nltk.word_tokenize to split a sentence with contractions and explains why it is advantageous.
candidates.lesson_title: Biblioteca de manipulação de texto: NLTK e Spacy

candidates.label: Handling Portuguese text encoding (ISO 8859-1)
candidates.description: Awareness that many Portuguese text resources use ISO 8859-1 encoding and how to decode such text in Python when reading files.
coverage_criteria: Explains why specifying encoding is necessary when opening Portuguese text files.
Decodes bytes using 'ISO 8859-1' encoding in Python.
candidates.lesson_title: Biblioteca de manipulação de texto: NLTK e Spacy

candidates.label: Stop Words Removal
candidates.description: Filtering out common words (e.g., 'the', 'is') that carry little semantic value, using predefined lists such as NLTK's stopwords.
coverage_criteria: Remove stop words from text using NLTK.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Basic Text Cleaning
candidates.description: Lowercasing text and removing HTML tags, special characters, and punctuation to reduce noise and ensure uniformity.
coverage_criteria: Explain why lowercasing and removing special characters helps text analysis.
Apply cleaning to a raw text sample.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Word-level Tokenization
candidates.description: Splitting raw text into individual words (tokens) as the first step of NLP pipelines, often using functions like d2l.tokenize.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Vocabulary Construction and Out-of-Vocabulary Handling
candidates.description: Building a vocabulary from training tokens with a minimum frequency filter, and ignoring unknown words during testing to avoid errors.
coverage_criteria: Create a vocabulary with frequency filters.
Explain the strategy for handling OOV words.
candidates.lesson_title: NLTK, BoW e Naive Bayes para Análise de Conteúdo

candidates.label: Pré-processamento para Word Embeddings
candidates.description: Etapas comuns de pré-processamento incluem conversão para minúsculas, remoção de pontuações e stop words, e tokenização, com o objetivo de uniformizar o texto antes da vetorização.
coverage_criteria: Liste as etapas típicas de pré-processamento para word embeddings.
Explique o propósito de cada etapa.

candidate_assignment_rule: Cluster only. Every input candidate ID must appear exactly once across clusters. Prefer tight clusters; topic overlap alone is not a cluster.

web_access_policy.instruction: Do not use web search or open URLs. Use only the provided candidate cards.
